title: Luxury Guests Keep One Hotel Group Strong

source.author: Montira Rungjirajittranon
source.title: Thai Luxury Leads Minor’s Quarter Despite Tourist Slump

paragraphs: This is a tale of two regions. Thailand expects fewer foreign tourists this year. Nevertheless, one hotel company is earning more money there. Minor Hotels reported its results for July to September. Its core profit rose 13 percent compared with a year earlier, to about 62.9 million dollars. Minor owes much of this to Thailand.

Thailand now expects 33 million international visitors in 2026, down from 36.7 million. Simultaneously, Minor's luxury hotels there, called Anantara, did remarkable business. In the third quarter, the money they made from each available room rose 19 percent. Room prices rose 13 percent on average. Across all of Minor's hotels in Thailand, this measure rose 13 percent, the best of any major market in the group.

Cushman & Wakefield, a property company, told Skift that luxury guests worry less about prices. Minor also owes part of its success to new spending. In September, it finished a 50 million dollar renovation of Anantara Siam Bangkok, with all 335 rooms refreshed. In the Maldives, where Minor runs nine resorts, the room measure rose 10 percent.

The other half of the tale is harsh. In the Middle East and Africa, the room measure fell 11 percent in the third quarter. Over nine months, it fell 15 percent. Minor blamed the conflict in the region and weaker travel demand. Marriott's room measure in the Middle East fell 12 percent in the quarter.

However, the problem hurts Minor more than its rivals. Marriott mostly relies on fees in the Middle East. The region brings only about 3 percent of its global fees. In contrast, Minor owns about 40 percent of its hotels in the Middle East and Africa. When those hotels earn less, its own profit falls directly. Across the whole group, almost 70 percent of Minor's hotels are owned or leased. With a lease, a company rents the building and runs the hotel itself.

In the Gulf, Minor's plan is to keep prices high rather than to fill more rooms. It does not want to compromise on price. But this is becoming harder. In the third quarter, room prices in the region fell for the first time this year.

Group CEO Dillip Rajakarier spoke about the value of a diverse group of hotels, because conditions are very different from one market to another. The company will be strict about margins and prices. Being strict means it will not compromise, even in a harsh market. It also wants to earn more from fees. More than 90 percent of its future hotels will not be owned by Minor. In nine months, it signed deals for 38 hotels. The 2025 record was 40.

For now, its results can rise in one region and fall in another simultaneously. Bookings for Thailand and the Maldives are ahead of last year for the end of 2026 and early 2027. A diverse group of hotels helps when one region has a harsh year.
